item.title: Driftflow 0.2.18
item.description:
New: the Stack. Add a dictation to it with the new button on the pill, or turn on Stack Mode to collect everything you say, then paste the lines one at a time, all at once, or drag them into any text box.

Pin lines you use again and again, keep a separate stack for each message or person, and see them all on the new Stacks page.

A dictation that ends where there's nothing to paste into (the desktop, a file list) now goes into your stack instead of being lost.

Transcribe Files now lists WhatsApp voice notes (.opus, .ogg), which work without anything extra on macOS 26.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.17
item.description:
Faster everywhere you dictate: with Vocabulary words, text appears up to 4× sooner after you let go of the key.

The pill and start sound appear the moment you press the key.

Your first words show up in the live preview sooner.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.16
item.description:
New versions now arrive within minutes of release. A window shows what's new with Install Now or Later, the menu bar icon gets a blue dot, and Restart to Update sits at the top of the menu.

If you choose Later, the update installs by itself when your Mac has been idle for 10 minutes or the screen locks, so you're never left on an old version.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.15
item.description: The main window opens and switches sections faster, however long your History gets: it shows 50 dictations at a time with Show More, and no longer redraws while you dictate.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.14
item.description: Tidier Files layout: no line through the title, a compact transcript header with the play time showing, and the window widens to fit.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.13
item.description:
Transcribing files is up to 4× faster on long recordings: a 34-minute file now takes about 9 seconds instead of 36.

Files now lives in the main window, next to History, with the settings below. The menu, Open With and dropping files on the Dock icon all open it there.

Choose which speech model transcribes your files, or transcribe any file again with another model to compare.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.12
item.description:
The style that keeps your words exactly as spoken is now called Original (it was Literal). Your choice and app rules carry over.

Check for Updates… now sits just above Quit in the menu.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.11
item.description: Dictating into Jump Desktop, Microsoft Remote Desktop, Screen Sharing and other remote-desktop apps pastes what you said, instead of whatever was last copied on the remote computer.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.10
item.description:
Bluetooth headsets and earbuds no longer make the microphone restart over and over during a dictation, which could lose what you said.

Fixed a rare crash in the background.

The About window shows what Driftflow is, with links to the website, what's new and reporting a problem.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.9
item.description:
A proper installer. Open the .dmg and drag Driftflow onto Applications. If Driftflow is opened from anywhere else, it offers to move itself to Applications.

The live preview now uses the same NVIDIA model as the final text, so what you see is exactly what gets typed. Apple Speech is still available under Settings › Models › Advanced.

The Professional and Casual styles now make a clearly visible difference, while still never answering or obeying what you dictate.

The Advanced sections in Settings are always open.

Copy Log now includes past sessions and summaries of recent crash reports, notes when a session ended unexpectedly, and Save Report… writes everything to a file.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.8
item.description: Fixes a crash in setup's microphone step on Macs whose microphones run at different sample rates (for example a Mac mini with a USB mic or AirPods). If a microphone still can't be opened, Driftflow now says so instead of quitting.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.7
item.description:
The Settings window's close, minimise and zoom buttons now sit inside the sidebar, like other macOS apps.

Moving between setup steps no longer slides the old step across the window or overlaps the titles.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.6
item.description:
Saying "drift flow" (or Drift-Flow, DriftFlow) is now always written Driftflow.

New Copy Log for Support, in the menu and in Settings, to send us what happened when something goes wrong. What you dictate is never in the log.

The setup and Settings windows can be minimised, zoomed and resized, and the setup window's buttons sit where you'd expect.

item.title: Driftflow 0.2.0
item.description:
The first public release of Driftflow for Mac: on-device dictation for Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 15 or later).

Hold Right ⌘ to dictate and release to insert; tap it once for hands-free. Nothing leaves your Mac.

From this version on, Driftflow updates itself.
